title: The Charm That Worked on Butterflies

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HUMOR AND ABSURDITY (HUM-01 to HUM-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Slapstick, silly noises, puns, pranks with permission, ridiculous coincidences, a little funny magic and animals being absurd. Nobody is the butt of the joke: everyone keeps their dignity, and the comedy needs no victim.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager's insect charm draws every butterfly in the garden instead: keep working, or take it back to the elder.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (elder), an elder, gave (subject) a little woven charm to keep biting insects away while (subject.he/she) works in the garden. It works. Not a single biting insect comes near (subject.him/her). Instead, every butterfly in the garden has landed on (subject): on (subject.his/her) shoulders, in (subject.his/her) hair, on (subject.his/her) nose. (subject.He/she) looks like a walking flower bed. Whether it is the charm, or the sweet sap on (subject.his/her) hands, nobody knows.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) carries on weeding, very slowly and gently, in a cloud of color. The children follow (subject.him/her) round the garden all afternoon. At sunset the butterflies lift off together and drift away. (subject) feels a little lonely without them. (subject.He/she) keeps the charm.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (elder) looks at (subject), butterflies and all, and says, "Ah. It does that sometimes." "Sometimes?" "It has never been quite sure what an insect is." (subject) decides that this is a fair thing to be confused about, and keeps it.
